name: Zeabur

modes.label: Bring or buy server; compute separately billed
modes.commit_note: Servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate and auto-renew until cancelled; sizes.hour = month/730.
modes.note: Fixed-price monthly servers resold by Zeabur (Tencent Lighthouse, Aliyun SWAS, DigitalOcean, Linode, Hetzner), cheapest plan per vCPU/RAM shape from the live catalog (api.zeabur.com dedicatedServerPlans, as used by zeabur.com/pricing); hour = monthly price/730. Prices vary by provider and city; US and EU entries are both listed (city in name). A Zeabur plan fee is charged on top.

storage.included_disk_gib: per server size (40-1280 GB; e.g. 4C8G Tencent 120 GB, Hetzner cpx32 160 GB)

network.egress_free_gib: per server size (e.g. Tencent 4C8G 3,584 GB/month, Hetzner EU 20,000 GB, DigitalOcean 4C8G 5,000 GB)

plans.name: Free
plans.note: CONFLICT: pricing page says buying a server needs a paid plan ('Paid subscription required'), docs/server FAQ says 'No, you do not need a subscription plan to use a server'. Refund policy: after downgrading to Free, 'your currently deployed containerized services will be automatically suspended by the system'. Free plan is non-commercial only (Fair Use).

caveats: Runtime server prices vary by selected marketplace provider and location.
14-day Dev/Pro trial is promotional; no permanent free compute inferred.
Unknowns remain null, not free; generic infrastructure modes are opt-in alt.
Worked example assumes resources are released between active windows unless a retained-instance scenario is explicitly discussed.
VAT basis: Unknown: reviewed pricing source does not explicitly establish VAT/tax inclusion.
Residency: Server marketplace lets users choose provider and city; selection determines runtime location. Control-plane/support residency not established.

Server billing mechanics: monthly prepaid, auto-renew charged from balance; on failed renewal the server is powered off (1 day after expiry for AWS Lightsail/GCP/Hetzner/Linode/DO; at expiry for Tencent/Aliyun/Volcengine) and deleted after ~7 / ~15 days. Upgrades are one-way (no downgrade). Refunds: prorated, as Zeabur credits; Tencent/Aliyun/Volcengine only one unconditional refund per account. Prepaid credits non-refundable. Zeabur resells Hetzner ABOVE Hetzner list (cpx32 $48 vs originalPrice $42.99) but Tencent/Aliyun/Linode below list.
Shared (usage-billed) cluster deprecated: no new projects; existing shared-cluster projects stopped accepting new services on 2026-04-01. All compute is now Servers (fixed monthly) or BYO servers.

Plan limits (pricing page): manageable own (BYO) servers Free 1 / Dev 3 / Pro 10 / Team unlimited; build CI 2C4G (Free/Dev) or 4C8G (Pro/Team); log retention 48h/7d/30d/90d. Dev and Pro: 14-day free trial ('$0 First 14 days free'). Team $79 = 3 seats, +$24/seat. Plan fees are on top of server costs.

fleet.verification: Free plan requires no credit card.
fleet.notes: Plan comparison distinguishes managed services, user-hosted servers and AI credits. No verified universal fresh-account machine/vCPU/GPU concurrency cap or quota-review SLA; services sleeping after inactivity do not imply account-wide fleet capacity.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Zeabur will start a new deployment using the most recent configuration.
snapshot_auto.note: Suspend (manual) and Free-plan auto-sleep ('Services on the Free Plan automatically sleep after a period of inactivity.') keep config and volumes but do not save process or root-filesystem state; resume is a fresh deployment. Automatic daily backups exist, but only for volumes/databases on Dev+ (7-day retention), and they are scheduled backups, not stop-snapshots.

egress_allowlist.quote: Outbound connections from your services are not restricted by the firewall.
egress_allowlist.note: Server firewall is inbound-only. (The Claude Code skills page loosely says 'Set inbound and outbound traffic rules for servers', but the firewall doc is explicit and no outbound feature is documented.) On a purchased server with SSH/root you could configure host iptables yourself, but that is guest-side.

egress_http_rules.quote: Outbound connections from your services are not restricted by the firewall.
egress_http_rules.note: No outbound controls of any kind, so none at HTTP level.

ingress_rules.quote: Zeabur provides server-level firewall management, allowing you to configure inbound rules directly from the Dashboard without SSH-ing into the server to manage iptables manually.
ingress_rules.note: Per-server inbound rules (TCP/UDP, port range, source IP/CIDR), default-deny ('Zeabur’s firewall uses an allowlist strategy (default-deny).'). Caveat on page: 'may still be under development or only available for certain servers'. The Gateway add-on adds IPv4 whitelist/blacklist ('Gateway supports IP-based access control to restrict who can access your services through the gateway.'). Per-service choice of which ports get domains / public host:port, plus private networking (*.zeabur.internal). No authenticated/tokenized URLs documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Zeabur provides server-level firewall management, allowing you to configure inbound rules directly from the Dashboard without SSH-ing into the server to manage iptables manually.
guest_firewall.note: Applies to Servers: full VPS (ZeaburOS=K3s, or plain Ubuntu 24.04) with SSH and sudo, so host iptables/nftables work (docs show sudo host operations). Must not block ports 22/80/443/4222/6443/30000-32767 on ZeaburOS. Inside deployed service containers, NET_ADMIN is not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Zeabur will automatically inject these environment variables into your service.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are plain service environment variables (with ${VAR} references). No credential-injecting egress proxy documented. Zeabur AI Hub (LLM gateway) issues a key that the app itself holds.

volume_attach.quote: On Zeabur, you can mount Volumes to persistently store your data within a service.
volume_attach.note: Per-service persistent volumes (Volume ID + mount dir; billed; disables zero-downtime restarts). On Dedicated Servers you can also mount an extra disk at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage (host-level, via SSH). Clusters offer 'Distributed volumes that can follow workloads across nodes'.

volume_shared.quote: Volumes are scoped to a single service and cannot be shared between services.
volume_shared.note: Docs recommend network object storage (MinIO/RustFS) for shared data. Cluster distributed volumes move with a workload; they are not documented as multi-writer.

isolation.quote: Pick a standard distribution and you get a standard VPS, exactly as the distribution ships it — just like one from any provider.
isolation.note: The card's 'managed-server' mode is Zeabur reselling whole dedicated VPS instances from Tencent Lighthouse, Aliyun SWAS, DigitalOcean, Linode, Hetzner, AWS, GCP, Volcengine — each a full single-tenant virtual machine with root/SSH access, not a shared container.

docker_inside.quote: You operate it entirely over SSH: what runs on it, how it is configured, and how it is maintained are all up to you.
docker_inside.note: Full root/SSH access to a standard VPS (or ZeaburOS, which itself runs K3s/containers); Docker is not explicitly named but a self-managed VPS with root normally supports it. Not directly confirmed in docs.

desktop.quote: Deploy and scale your app with zero configuration.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (PaaS/VPS-reselling deployment platform, no managed graphical desktop).

browser.quote: Deploy and scale your app with zero configuration.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: Deploy and scale your app with zero configuration.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Deploy and scale your app with zero configuration.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: Deploy and scale your app with zero configuration.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Fixed IP Server — for connecting your own server with a fixed public IP via SSH
egress_ip_type.note: Purchased/added servers are dedicated cloud-provider VPS instances with a fixed datacenter public IP, used for both inbound and outbound traffic.

ssh.quote: full SSH access to the host remains available

snapshot.quote: “Backup” will only back up the data within the volumes; other files in the service (such as source code) will not be backed up.
snapshot.note: No full machine/disk snapshot capability for purchased servers is documented; only per-service mounted-volume/database backups exist, and those are scoped to the deploy-service mode, not the whole VPS.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Zeabur only retains your backups for 7 days.
snapshot_on_demand.note: On-demand backup exists for volumes/databases (via dashboard button or GraphQL query), not for a whole machine/server snapshot.

fork.quote: Purchased servers are fully managed by Zeabur.
fork.note: No machine-cloning/fork feature is documented for servers; project-level 'Copy Project' exists for the deploy-service mode but does not clone a running/VM machine state.

fork_running.quote: Purchased servers are fully managed by Zeabur.
fork_running.note: not offered: no fork/clone capability of any kind is documented for servers.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Purchased servers are fully managed by Zeabur.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: no memory-preserving clone/snapshot feature documented.

pause_resume.quote: Purchased servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate. ... Your server will auto-renew unless you cancel it.
pause_resume.note: Servers are fixed-monthly-billed VPS instances; there is no documented pause that reduces billing (billing continues regardless of running state until cancellation/expiry).

wake_on_request.quote: Purchased servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for the dedicated-server mode (always-on VPS, no serverless wake-on-request).

auto_stop_idle.quote: Purchased servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate.
auto_stop_idle.note: Dedicated VPS servers run continuously and are billed at a fixed monthly rate regardless of idle time; no auto-stop-on-idle is documented for this mode (Free-plan idle sleep applies only to the deploy-service PaaS mode, not purchased servers).

live_resize.quote: Yes, you can self-serve upgrade your server plan from the server’s settings page. Note that upgrades are one-way — you cannot downgrade to a lower plan after upgrading.
live_resize.note: Plan upgrade is possible but is a one-way plan change, not documented as a live, no-downtime CPU/RAM resize of a running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: Zeabur’s official Claude Code plugin converts natural language into infrastructure operations. Deploy services, rent servers, manage configurations — all without leaving your editor.
agent_harnesses.note: This is a client-side Claude Code plugin that lets a user control Zeabur (rent servers, deploy) from their own Claude Code session; it is not a coding-agent harness preinstalled/offered as a template running inside Zeabur's sandboxes/servers.

harness_api.quote: Zeabur’s official Claude Code plugin converts natural language into infrastructure operations.
harness_api.note: No first-party API to prompt/stream a coding harness running inside a Zeabur machine; the plugin drives Zeabur's own API from the user's local Claude Code, the reverse direction.

own_agent_api.quote: Deploy and scale your app with zero configuration.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent product).

mcp_server.quote: Zeabur provides an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows you to manage and deploy your Zeabur projects in AI applications that support MCP.

lang_python.quote: Purchased servers are fully managed by Zeabur.
lang_python.note: Standard Linux VPS/ZeaburOS with root+SSH access runs any language runtime you install; Zeabur's docs also list first-party Python framework guides (Django, Flask, Reflex) confirming Python support out of the box for the platform.

lang_node.quote: Purchased servers are fully managed by Zeabur.
lang_node.note: Standard Linux VPS/ZeaburOS with root+SSH access runs any language runtime you install; Zeabur's docs also list first-party Node.js framework guides (Express, NestJS, Next.js, etc.) confirming Node.js support out of the box for the platform.

public_ipv4.quote: Fixed IP Server — for connecting your own server with a fixed public IP via SSH
public_ipv4.note: Every purchased server is a dedicated VPS instance with its own public IPv4 address.

inbound_https.quote: By default, Zeabur opens the ports required for services to operate (such as 80 and 443)
inbound_https.note: Custom domains get automatic HTTPS certificate provisioning per the security-practices page.

static_egress_ip.quote: Fixed IP Server — for connecting your own server with a fixed public IP via SSH
static_egress_ip.note: A dedicated VPS's fixed public IP is used for both inbound and outbound (egress) traffic.

windows.quote: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is available today, and more operating systems and versions will be added over time.
windows.note: Only Linux distributions (ZeaburOS/Ubuntu) are offered; no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.quote: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is available today, and more operating systems and versions will be added over time.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Linux-only server catalog resold from AWS/GCP/Hetzner/Linode/DigitalOcean/Aliyun/Tencent/Volcengine).

self_host.quote: A platform that helps you deploy services with one click.
self_host.note: The zeabur/zeabur GitHub repo contains only docs/schema/CLI-plugin assets, not the platform's control-plane source; no self-hosted/on-prem version of the Zeabur SaaS control plane is documented.

open_source.quote: A platform that helps you deploy services with one click.
open_source.note: Zeabur open-sources framework templates, zbpack (buildpack) and CLI/docs tooling, but the core SaaS dashboard/control plane itself is not published as open source.

soc2.quote: Zeabur is currently pursuing SOC 2 Type II certification.
soc2.note: Not yet attested as of the docs' last update; certification is in progress, not completed.

hipaa.quote: Zeabur is currently pursuing SOC 2 Type II certification. Our compliance program covers the Trust Services Criteria for security, availability, and confidentiality.
hipaa.note: HIPAA/BAA is not mentioned anywhere on the security/compliance page; no HIPAA eligibility or BAA offering is documented.

sso.quote: All employees authenticate through Google Workspace with two-factor authentication (2FA) enforced.
sso.note: That line describes Zeabur's own internal employee auth, not a customer-facing SAML/OIDC SSO offering; no customer SSO feature is documented in the team-management docs.

eu_data_residency.quote: Region — Filter by continent (Asia, China, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania).
eu_data_residency.note: Servers can be purchased in European cities (e.g. Frankfurt, London, Nuremberg per the live catalog), so a customer can keep their machine/data in the EU.

max_session_h.quote: Purchased servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate. ... Your server will auto-renew unless you cancel it.
max_session_h.note: A dedicated VPS runs indefinitely until the customer stops/cancels it or fails to pay renewal; there is no maximum session-length cutoff.

usage_api.quote: Zeabur's API is built on GraphQL, powering the Dashboard, CLI, and all first-party products. REST endpoints are also available for specific operations (file uploads, container operations, etc.). GraphQL API: Project / Service / Environment management, deployments, logs.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; No usage/billing API endpoint documented. Purchased servers are billed monthly at fixed rates. Shared cluster (deprecated) was usage-billed but deprecated. Usage/cost visibility only through dashboard, not via GraphQL, REST, or CLI APIs.
